summary.headline: The Trails Committee debated floor amendment and outreach strategies to salvage CPA funding for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge at Town Meeting.
summary.summary: The Southborough Trails Committee met to prepare for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, focusing on Warrant Article 4 for the Peninsula Trail Phase 2 pedestrian bridge. With the Select Board and Advisory Committee both voting not to recommend the article, members debated whether to offer a floor amendment to reduce the request to $25,000 in new CPA funds while repurposing $211,000 in previously allocated CPA funds and pursuing a $100,000 MassTrails grant. The committee also finalized preparations for an upcoming guided hike, trail yoga sessions, and public outreach at Heritage Day.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and approved the meeting minutes from September 17, 2026.
key_details: Minutes from September 17, 2026 were presented by the secretary.
The committee approved the minutes without edits.

topics.title: Fall trail events and youth hunting season safety
topics.summary: The chair reviewed upcoming community programming on town trails, including yoga sessions and a guided hike. Safety protocols were discussed due to the concurrent opening of youth hunting season, and the committee coordinated a November food drive.
key_details: Yoga on the Trails and a guided hike scheduled for Saturday, October 3, 2026.
Hikers are urged to wear blaze orange due to youth hunting season opening; safety vests will be borrowed from the Recreation Department.
Parking for the October 3 hike was secured at the Southborough Historical Society.
A trail run/walk and Southborough Food Pantry food drive are planned for November 7, 2026.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 2 Town Meeting funding strategy
topics.summary: The committee held an extensive strategic debate on how to present Warrant Article 4 at the October 17 Special Town Meeting after receiving negative recommendation votes from the Select Board (1-4) and Advisory Committee (0-7). The chair proposed preparing a fallback floor amendment that would reallocate $211,000 in previously granted CPA funds exclusively to the pedestrian bridge, add only $25,000 in new CPA funds, and seek a $100,000 MassTrails grant to complete the approximately $330,000 bridge. Members debated whether floating alternative funding ideas publicly would weaken the main proposal, while also drafting an informational FAQ document addressing cost, connectivity, and environmental value.
key_details: The committee was granted a 5-minute presentation slot at Town Meeting for Article 4.
A proposed fallback amendment would repurpose $211,000 in existing CPA funds and request $25,000 in new CPA funds rather than the full $217,000 previously sought.
The pedestrian bridge would eliminate a hazardous pedestrian walk along Route 30 lacking shoulders and guardrails.
The bridge connects to regional systems including the 33-mile Boroughs Loop Trail, 230-mile Bay Circuit Trail, and the Aqueduct Trail.
Members discussed countering opposition arguments that CPA funds should be prioritized for athletic fields instead of trails.
topics.outcome: The committee agreed to refine the voter FAQ sheet, add trail maps, and consult further with the Community Preservation Committee regarding floor amendment logistics.
topics.why_it_matters: The outcome of Article 4 at Town Meeting will decide whether Southborough completes the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge or forfeits previously designated CPA funding for the project.

topics.title: Public outreach and Heritage Day planning
topics.summary: Members discussed ways to publicize Town Meeting and the trail article to residents before voting day. Plans include setting up an informational table outside Town Meeting, borrowing promotional A-frame signs, and hosting a committee booth at Heritage Day.
key_details: Committee plans to borrow six A-frame signs from the Southborough Rotary Club to advertise Town Meeting and trail information.
Signs will be placed at high-visibility locations such as Town Hall, the library, and key roadway intersections.
The committee will host an informational booth at Heritage Day on Monday, October 12, 2026, from 9:00 AM to roughly 2:00 PM.
Members will staff an informational table outside the Town Meeting venue one hour prior to the meeting.
topics.outcome: Members will coordinate sign printing and arrange booth staffing for Heritage Day.
